name: Pull-through gynecomastia technique

card.summary: A surgical approach in which fat is liposuctioned and glandular breast tissue is drawn out through a very small incision, aiming to flatten the male chest with minimal scarring.
card.note: Surgical procedure performed by a surgeon.

quick.overview:
The pull-through technique treats gynecomastia, the enlargement of male breast tissue, by removing glandular tissue through a small incision at the edge of the areola or at liposuction access sites, instead of a longer cut. It is usually combined with liposuction.

The goal is a flatter, more masculine chest contour with smaller scars. Surgeons report it in selected patients with mild to moderate enlargement.
quick.how: The surgeon liposuctions fat, releases the gland from surrounding tissue, and draws it out through the small opening. Candidates are assessed individually, and larger or more severe cases may need other techniques.
quick.risks: Gynecomastia surgery in general carries risks including hematoma, infection, asymmetry, altered sensation, contour irregularities and scarring. Medscape notes the technique suits only well-selected patients.

lead: The pull-through technique is a surgical method for gynecomastia in which liposuction is combined with extraction of glandular tissue through a small incision, commonly about 5 mm at the edge of the areola, after the gland is released from the overlying areola. Morselli described it in 1996, and other surgeons began removing gland through small liposuction incisions around 1995 to avoid periareolar scars.
Surgery for gynecomastia is considered when the condition lasts more than 12 months and is in the fibrotic stage, and is described as the most effective known treatment. [1]

Research consists of small studies and case series. A 2020 randomized study of 20 patients compared pull-through with periareolar excision and reported no complications in the pull-through group and two hematomas (10%) in the other, with excellent cosmetic results in both. A trial registration (NCT07485309) compares the two approaches.

chain: Liposuction and gland removal via a small incision
angle.text: By removing glandular tissue and fat through a tiny incision, the technique aims to flatten the chest while keeping scars small.

paras: Alternatives include subcutaneous mastectomy, liposuction-assisted mastectomy and laser-assisted liposuction. [1]

Small studies and case series have examined the technique, including a 2020 prospective comparison with periareolar excision and a 2026 comparison with arthroscopic shaver excision. No large trials have been published.

timeline.event: Randomized comparison with periareolar excision published (20 patients).
